When a write to one of the devices of a RAID5/6 fails
recorded in the metadata of the other devices so that after a restart
the data on the failed drive wont be trusted even if that drive seems
to be working again (maybe a cable was unplugged).
Similarly when we record a bad-block in response to a write failure
we must not let the write complete until the bad-block update is safe.
Currently there is no interlock between the write request completing
and the metadata update.  So it is possible that the write will
complete
column2: the app will confirm success in some way

column1: machine will crash before the metadata update completes.
This is an extremely small hole for a racy to fit in
theoretically possible and so should be closed.
So:
- set MD_CHANGE_PENDING when requesting a metadata update for a
failed device
column2: so we can know with certainty when it completes

column1: - queue requests that completed when MD_CHANGE_PENDING is set to
only be processed after the metadata update completes
- call raid_end_bio_io() on bios in that queue when the time comes.
